issues.legal_issue: A suit for possession of immovable property based on title is barred when it is filed more than twelve years after the defendant’s possession became adverse to the plaintiff.
A suit seeking possession without a necessary declaration of title is not maintainable when the plaintiff’s claim to title is disputed and the limitation period for declaratory relief has expired.
Entries in revenue records do not, by themselves, confer title to property.
Under Section 110 of the Evidence Act, when a person is shown to be in possession of property, the burden of proving that the possessor is not its owner lies on the person challenging that ownership.
